---
title: "Human-in-the-Loop"
description: "An approach that includes people in an AI system's data, review, decision, or feedback process."
term: "Human-in-the-Loop"
letter: "H"
category: "AI Engineering"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

Human-in-the-loop systems involve people in parts of an AI workflow.
People may label examples, review model outputs, provide corrections,
or make the final decision.

## Technical explanation

Human involvement can occur during data collection, active learning,
quality assurance, exception handling, or deployment decisions. The
workflow should specify what information reviewers see, what authority
they have, how disagreements are resolved, and how feedback is recorded.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Human review can provide oversight where model errors are costly or
uncertainty is high. Poorly designed review can create automation bias,
excessive workload, inconsistent labels, or a false impression that a
system is safe simply because a person is nominally present.

## How it works

The system routes selected cases to reviewers, presents relevant
context and model outputs, and records the human decision. Routing
criteria, escalation paths, review capacity, and feedback use should
be evaluated as part of the end-to-end system.

## Practical example

A document-processing service can automatically handle routine cases
and send low-confidence or high-impact cases to a trained reviewer
before finalizing the result.

## Common misconceptions

- Human review is not automatically effective; reviewers need enough
  time, context, and authority.
- A human-in-the-loop process does not remove the need to evaluate the
  model or workflow.
- Reviewers may be influenced by model suggestions, especially when
  those suggestions are presented with unjustified confidence.
